name: Pawl: App Blocker With a Key

ios.desc:
Most blockers can be turned off by the same person who set them up, in about thirty seconds, at the exact moment they most want to. Pawl is built for that moment.

Pawl blocks the apps and websites you choose. Social feeds, games, shopping, news, adult sites, betting, anything. It uses Apple's Screen Time. The block screen has no unlock button. To open anything, you need your key.

HOW IT WORKS
- Pick what to block. Choose apps in Apple's own Screen Time picker, type in websites, or turn on a website category.
- Pair a security key. Plug in a physical FIDO2 security key once. Then put it somewhere hard to reach.
- To unblock, you need the key. Then you wait 15 minutes before anything opens. After that, the block comes back on by itself.
- You can make the wait longer at any time. Making it shorter is delayed too.

YOUR KEY IS YOUR ACCOUNTABILITY
Whoever holds your key decides when Pawl can open. Give it to a sister or friend across town, put it in a time lock box, a bank safe deposit box, or your desk at work. They don't need to install anything.

A real example: it is 1am and you open the app you told yourself you were done with. You see Pawl's block screen. Your key is at your sister's place across town. By the time you could get it and wait out the 15 minutes, the urge has usually passed. That is the whole idea.

FOR THE HARD MOMENTS
- An "I'm tempted" button: a ten-minute wait, your own notes from past moments, how many times you have resisted, and a one-tap call to someone you trust. It never leads to an unblock.
- A streak that survives deleting the app. It lives in your iCloud.
- A private log. Slips are part of changing a habit, and nothing in Pawl scolds you for one.

WHILE PAWL IS PROTECTING YOU
- Pawl turns on Screen Time's block on deleting apps, so deleting Pawl is not a quick way out.
- Pawl asks Screen Time to require automatic date and time, which is meant to stop you from moving the clock ahead to skip the wait.

PAWL PRO
- Scheduled sets: a Work set that blocks social apps 9 to 5 on weekdays, or an Evenings set for after 8pm. When a set's hours end, its apps open on their own. Up to ten sets. Making a set block less needs your key and the wait.
- The weekly report: the days Pawl was on, hours back, blocked attempts, urges resisted, the time of day that was hardest, and your own words from the week. It never scores or grades you.

HONEST ABOUT THE LIMITS
Pawl adds friction. It is not a cage.
- iOS lets the owner of a phone turn Screen Time

show_hn.title: Show HN: Pawl – iOS gambling blocker you unlock with a physical Security Key

quotes.text:
Hi HN!

I built this to make unblocking apps on your phone a lot harder. You add a physical key, then put it out of reach or give it to a friend, so unblocking becomes a real hassle. I started out wanting to build software around hardware security keys. My thinking was that they belong in high stakes moments, where proving it's really you matters the most.

One of those scenarios is gambling/unblocking apps on your phone. A hardware key is a physical thing you have to go find, plug in, and tap. That makes it a good fit for moments where the user isn't 100% sure they want to unblock something. Gambling is one of those moments. You can lose a lot of money when nobody else has to verify/authenticate your behavior.

So I built Pawl. You can use it alone, or with a sponsor/spouse/partner who approves each unlock. It uses Apple's built in Screen Time API, enabling you to block adult sites, gambling, and/or apps of your choosing.

There is no unlock button in the app, you have to plug in your security key (that you put out of reach) and authenticate that you truly want to unblock apps/websites. After that, you wait 15 minutes. Then the block will turn back on after 30 minutes. This is customizable. Your clean day streak is saved in iCloud, so deleting the app doesn't reset it.
